_comment: The pre-registration of agent_architecture.md §7's last reporting rule: budget
and hyperparameters are fixed before any test run, all method debugging happens
on train, and every arm is reported on test — never 'best of'. Committed before
the registered search and before any test rollout; its sha256 travels with every
run (harness/preregistration.py), so an edit after the fact moves the hash rather
than quietly redefining what was promised. Amendments are appended to
'amendments' with their reason, never applied by rewriting a value in place.

what_it_produced: One registered search over train: selection score 0.8285555 → 0.9023333 across
540 rollouts and 6 candidates at €0.7571, all 540 served by gmicloud. Per
abstention 0.920 → 0.950, card_recall 0.950 → 0.900. Its winner is registered
at versions 11/12 and the run is MLflow 546f3dfad8304722b65b9c5d6320a299.
NO MEASUREMENT. The measurement run was stopped by operator decision roughly
fifteen minutes in, before ANY of the eighteen conditions completed and before
any file was written to eval/measurements/. Registration 3 therefore has a
train selection score and no test number, and its optimized arm was never
measured. Nothing about that partial run informs anything below: it produced
no score, no candidate and no comparison.
why_a_fourth_one: Registration 3 weakened the SEED to open headroom and got less than it aimed
for. Cutting the candidate surface 84% — 30,296 to 4,964 characters, every
routing rule and argument description deleted — moved the blended train
selection score only 0.844 → 0.829. The per-scorer split showed why the
aggregate barely moved: abstention fell 0.070 and answer fell about 0.03, while
card_recall ROSE 0.075, because that metric scores the union of every
lookup_reference call in a run and an unguided agent calls it more often. Half
the real degradation was cancelled inside the 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 blend.
The deeper obstacle is the one T134 named and registration 3 could not fix by
editing text: deepseek-v4-flash answers this suite at ~0.82 whatever the prompt
says. §8 puts the suite's sensitivity at 20 percentage points, and a model that
starts 18 points from the ceiling cannot show one.
So this registration moves the STUDENT rather than the seed. On a 30-record
train probe, ministral-8b-2512 on the same weakened seed answers 0.467 against
deepseek's 0.786 — a 32-point drop on the metric the thesis reports, which is
headroom of the size §8 says the suite can actually resolve.
It also resolves, for the first time in four registrations, the deviation §5
cares most about: the proposer is no longer the model under test.

commit_note: Registration 3's commit — the weakened seed, its pins and registration 3
itself. This registration and the model swap land in the ONE commit after it,
and no rollout of this registration exists against either. Naming the preceding
commit is what registrations 2 and 3 did and for the same reason: a
registration cannot carry the hash of the commit it is inside.
registered_against.case_files_note: Byte-identical to registrations 1, 2 and 3. Four registrations, one suite.

the_student: ONE INTENDED CHANGE. A dated snapshot, so §5's pin still names something the
the_proposer: reflection_model: UNCHANGED at deepseek-v4-flash-0731 — which, because the
student moved, now makes teacher and student DIFFERENT MODELS. This is not a
second intervention; it is the first registration in which §5's requirement is
met rather than deviated from. See `models.two_models_at_last`.
the_provider_pin: served_by: 'gmicloud' → 'gmicloud,mistral'. Forced, not chosen: the pin is
process-wide and the run now spans two models that share no provider. See
what_did_not_move: THE SEED. The weakened candidate surface stays exactly as registration 3 left
it, at versions 9/10, 4,964 characters, with the answer contract byte-identical
and T136's callable-naming sentence in all six tool texts. Reverting it would
have made this a different experiment.
The frozen text-to-SQL chain — sub-agent, builder and fixer all stay on
deepseek. Deliberate: that sub-agent's prompt is FROZEN (§3.1) and outside the
candidate surface, so a weak model there would add `upstream` exclusions no
prompt candidate could repair, and per-arm exclusion divergence is what §7's
repeat condition voids a run on. The cost of the choice is stated in
The suite, the splits, the repeats, the pairing, the bootstrap and its seed,
the two gaps, the win/loss table, the exclusion rule, the diagnostics, the
capture neighbourhood, the selection weights, the search budget, the budget
limit and the whole protocol section.

note: Registration 3's section applies verbatim and is not restated. The surface is
4,964 characters against the hand-written 30,296; the answer contract and its
no-clarification clause are byte-identical to every earlier run; T136's
sentence is in all six tool texts; lookup_reference's topic enum reaches the
model through the signature regardless of the docstring.
It matters MORE here. A weakened seed on a capable model cost 1.5 blended
points; on an 8B model the same seed costs 18. The interaction is the finding,
and it is why this run is not comparable with registration 3's and is not

two_models_at_last: §5 asks for a reflection model DISTINCT from the model under test, so that a
result can be attributed to one of the two. Registrations 2 and 3 both had to
declare a deviation from it: one served model in both roles, a search of a
model reflecting on its own rollouts, and a null that could never be pinned on
the proposer rather than the student.
That deviation is GONE here, as a side effect of moving the student rather than
as a separate intervention. The proposer is a capable model and the student is
an 8B one — strong teacher, weak student, which is the configuration prompt
The attribution this buys is narrow and worth stating exactly: a gain can no
longer be explained as the proposer scoring its own work, and a null can no
longer be explained as the proposer being as weak as the student. Neither
statement was available in any earlier run.
why_a_whitelist_is_still_a_pin: The provider pin is process-wide; the model is not. `mistral` serves no
deepseek and `gmicloud` serves no Ministral, so no single slug can carry a run
that spans both, and the pin is a two-member whitelist with
It remains HARD because the intersection of the whitelist with each model's
provider set is a SINGLETON — verified live against OpenRouter's endpoint
listing, not assumed: ministral-8b-2512 → mistral, deepseek-v4-flash-0731 →
gmicloud. `scripts/check_pins.py` performs that verification on every run and
FAILS on a whitelist it cannot verify or one whose intersection has two
members, because 'unverifiable' and 'pinned' must not print the same way. A
second member would restore the call-by-call mixing T134 introduced the field
to close, and the committed pin records the list rather than the resolution, so
The `served_by` string in the four model pins therefore names the WHITELIST and
not the server. `resolved_served_by` above names the servers, and the check is
what keeps the two in agreement.

provider_screen.note: Carried forward from registration 3 for deepseek; Ministral needed none.
provider_screen.gmicloud: deepseek: clean, 4.2 s mean — SELECTED for the SQL chain and the proposer
provider_screen.deepinfra: deepseek: clean at 4.4 s but `engine_overloaded` in bursts under a hard pin (registration 2, amendment 2)
provider_screen.relace: deepseek: cheapest and unusable — inlines the chain of thought into `content`, where the SQL builder reads its query
provider_screen.mistral: ministral-8b-2512: the ONLY provider, across three tags (mistral, mistral/zdr, mistral/eu). There is no routing choice to screen and no swap hazard to close — which is the one respect in which this model is easier to pin than deepseek.

note: Measured on train before this registration was written, because two properties
of an 8B student decide whether the run measures anything at all, and guessing
at them would have made the registration a wish. 30 train records, base program
only, 67 rollouts, €0.0911. No test split was touched.
parse_failure_rate: 2 of 67 rollouts = 3.0%. This is the number that decided the run was worth
doing. The contract block is preserved byte-for-byte, but an 8B model does not
always obey it — one observed failure was the model echoing the instruction
'Your final message is one JSON object and nothing else' as its answer.
3% is small enough that the baseline arm measures the prompt rather than the
harness. Had it been large, the run would not have been registered.
comparison_note: Against registration 3's seed scores over 100 records: answer 0.786,
two are 30 records and 100 records of the same split and are NOT paired, so the
differences describe rather than estimate. Answer is the one that matters and
The probe also moved 0.6474 → 0.8274 within a 32-call budget. That is a
selection score on the instances it selected over, at a budget one fifteenth of
the registered one, and it is NOT a preview of the result. It is recorded
because it was seen before registration and concealing it would be the thing

budget.available_note: Derived: registration 3's 19.1 less its own ledger (≈1.1 for the search, the smokes and the aborted measurement). The repository's arithmetic, not a balance read from the provider.

basis: Measured on the 30-record probe: 67 rollouts, 799,644 tokens, $0.0911 —
$0.00136 per rollout at ~11,900 tokens per rollout. Registration 3's search
took 540 rollouts and its measurement 1,686, so 540 × $0.00136 ≈ $0.73 and
Ministral costs MORE per token than deepseek ($0.15/$0.15 against $0.08/$0.18
per Mtok) and LESS per rollout, because it emits no reasoning trace: ~11,900
tokens against deepseek's ~21,000. The ledger blends both models, the SQL
The limit stays 6.0, unchanged across registrations 2, 3 and 4. The estimate
is a floor: a weaker student may take more steps per rollout, and the
optimized arm's candidate will be longer than the seed.

budget.if_exhausted: The split order in `measurement.splits` decides what is lost, as it has since registration 1's amendment 3.
ledger_price_caveat: These are DEEPSEEK's rates and the ledger applies them to every rollout,
Ministral's included, whose true rate is $0.15/$0.15. The ledger therefore
under-prices the root agent's input and over-prices its output. The figures
above are the ledger's own, so they are internally consistent and are not the
invoice. Left unchanged rather than patched mid-experiment: the price table is
a registered value and correcting it would move a registered number for a

baseline: The weakened seed at the pinned candidate_prompt_versions — root instruction
v9, the five tool docstrings at v9/v10, the sub-agent description at v9 —
answered by ministral-8b-2512. Registered once and read twice, so the reference
arm and the search's seed cannot drift apart.
It is a deliberately degraded prompt on a deliberately small model and its
absolute scores are NEVER quoted as the assistant's performance. It is the
floor the gain is measured from and nothing else.
It carries T107's known defect UNCHANGED and registered in advance, as every
registration since the first has had to: T17a enters at 0.50 abstention
accuracy, failing 3/3 with correct reasoning and a wrong contract encoding,
and T107 left it for the search because the encoding lives in the optimizable
text. The contract block is byte-identical to T107's here, so the defect is
neither repaired nor deepened by the weakening; a candidate that fixes it is
measuring what the thesis claims to measure, and this sentence exists so that
the improvement cannot later be read as a baseline quietly weakened to make
room for it. On this student it compounds with the 3.0% parse-failure rate,
which is a different failure of the same contract and is counted separately.
It is not comparable with any earlier registration's baseline. Registration 3
moved the text; this one moves the model.
optimized: Whatever candidate the one registered search selects, starting from that same
seed and proposed by deepseek-v4-flash. Not the best of several searches, not
the best iteration by test score, not a hand-picked candidate.
Registration 3's winner (versions 11/12) is NOT this arm and is not carried
over. It was selected against a different student and a candidate optimized for
one model is not the candidate for another; a fresh search is the only thing
that makes the pair a measurement.

budget_held_fixed: 500 metric calls, the same number registrations 2 and 3 ran. A weaker student
is a reason to want a larger budget and the reason not to take one: comparing
gains across the three runs requires the budget to be the thing that did not
llm_cache_hygiene: `.cache/llm` is CLEARED before the registered search, and clearing means
REMOVING THE DIRECTORY'S CONTENTS, not deleting `cache.db`: the store is
sharded into subdirectories and a file delete leaves entries behind. The cache
is keyed on the request, which includes the model id, so a Ministral call
cannot collide with a deepseek one — but the pilot runs above were the same
model on the same prompts, and those would replay.

measurement.pairing: the identical committed cases, in file order, for every arm and every repeat
repeats_note: Three, unchanged since registration 2. The repeats ARE the replication and are
what makes the LLM cache's being off matter. Registration 2 measured 0.135 of
test_seen cases disagreeing across repeats on a capable model; an 8B student
may be noisier, and this run measures that rather than assuming it.

why_it_is_not_widened: Registration 2 lost 43 and 39 of 375 test_seen rollouts and 66 and 65 of 168
test_unseen rollouts to `upstream`, nearly all cache misses on windows a
candidate chose. The counts CONVERGED between the arms, which is the property
§7 reads, so the neighbourhood is left alone.
A weaker student may choose stranger windows and miss more often. If the
per-arm counts diverge, §7's repeat condition fires and this run is repeated
rather than reported — registered here, before the counts exist.

analysis.repeat_reduction: mean over the repeats per case, before any aggregation over cases
analysis.primary_estimand: the paired difference optimized - baseline, per metric, on test_seen
analysis.test_unseen_trajectory: per-template win/loss table; no accuracy and no interval
analysis.abstention: accuracy over the unanswerable cases and the false-abstention rate over the answerable ones, reported separately and never blended
analysis.exclusion: harness_error cases leave every aggregate and are counted per arm with their sources broken out; invalid_argument never excludes
parse_failure: FIRST-ORDER IN THIS RUN, and read before any other number. The pilot measured
3.0% on the seed. §7 keeps it apart from answer accuracy so that an optimizer
degrading the output format stays distinguishable from one degrading
reasoning — and here the interesting direction is the opposite one: a candidate
that makes an 8B model hold the JSON contract is a real improvement, and it
would show up as answer accuracy unless this number is read beside it.
Reported per arm. If the baseline's rate is far above 3% the run is reported as
measuring the contract's legibility to a small model as much as the routing.
analysis.residual_nondeterminism: MEASURED, from the three repeats per condition. Every arm difference is read against it, and a difference smaller than it is within the noise floor rather than a small effect.
analysis.multiplicity: no correction across the four metrics. They are four declared quantities, not a family searched over for a winner.
card_recall_caveat: Registration 3's search found card_recall moving OPPOSITE to every other
metric — the weakened seed scored 0.950 and the optimized candidate 0.900. The
metric scores the union of every lookup_reference call in a run, so an
unselective agent scores higher, and a candidate that routes more deliberately
can lose recall while improving. It carries 0.1 of the selection weight and is
reported with this caveat attached wherever it moves down.
comparison_with_earlier_registrations: REPORTED SIDE BY SIDE, NEVER POOLED AND NEVER DIFFERENCED. Three runs now exist
with three different configurations: registration 2 (strong model, strong
seed, measured, gain +0.011 on test_seen answer), registration 3 (strong model,
weak seed, search only, train gain +0.074) and this one (weak model, weak seed).
Between any two of them more than one thing moved.
What the three carry jointly is a BRACKET, not an estimate: how much prompt
optimization adds depends on how much room the seed and the model leave, and
these are three points on that surface. The thesis reports them as three
measurements of a dependence, never as one effect size with an interval.
Registration 3 has no test number at all and is reported as a train selection
score with that stated, never alongside a test figure as though comparable.
what_a_null_would_mean: A null here is the strongest negative result available from this testbed. The
seed has 18 points of headroom on the blended score and 32 on answer accuracy,
the proposer is a capable model distinct from the student, and the budget is
the one that produced a +0.074 train gain in registration 3. If the optimizer
cannot move a weak student on a stripped prompt under those conditions, the
remaining explanations are T132's missing span half and the suite's own
A LARGE gain is the outcome the design expects and is therefore the one to
state most carefully: it would be a gain from a degraded seed on a small model,
and it does not transfer to either the hand-written seed or the capable model.
Registration 2 already measured that combination and found +0.011.
Neither outcome licenses a fifth registration that weakens something further

method_debugging: train only. The pilot above is train. The two test splits have been run once,
under registrations 1 and 2, and their numbers are in findings.md.
Nothing in this registration is chosen on a test number. The model was chosen
on a train probe of its answer accuracy and its parse-failure rate; the
provider follows from which providers serve the model; the budget, the suite,
the splits, the repeats, the bootstrap and the analysis are copied unchanged.
reporting: Both arms on all three splits, whatever the numbers are, and labelled a
weak-student headroom experiment wherever they appear. Neither arm's absolute
score is quoted as the assistant's performance: one is a degraded prompt on an
8B model and the other is a machine-written prompt on an 8B model.
§7's repeat condition applies unchanged. Diverging newly-recorded cache entry
counts are reported and never repaired.
stopping: The measurement is complete when both arms have three repeats on all three
splits. It is not stopped early on a favourable interval and not extended on an
unfavourable one. One search, one measurement, one report.

known_gaps.what: The reflective dataset reaches GEPA without its span half: MLflow stands down from tracing when ADK is already tracing, so the search reflects on `Feedback.rationale` and the inputs, not on the ADK tool spans.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED. Declared rather than waited for, as in registrations 2 and 3.
known_gaps.effect: The proposer sees less about a rollout than the design intends. It bounds a null here harder than in either earlier run, because this run's claim rests on a capable proposer being able to rediscover routing — and it can only infer it from rationales.

known_gaps.what: The proposer is asked to rewrite, not to revise, and nothing checks a candidate naming a callable no toolset resolves.
known_gaps.status: NOT FIXED. Checked by hand instead, per registration 3.
known_gaps.effect: Registration 3's winner was checked and was CLEAN: its one mention of `agent_tool_text_to_sql_agent` was a sentence forbidding its use — 'a registry label, not a callable, and must never be used as a tool name' — which is T136's seed-side sentence working. The same by-hand check is run on this run's winner and reported in findings.md.

known_gaps.what: The root agent is an 8B model while the frozen text-to-SQL chain it delegates to is a capable one.
known_gaps.effect: The system under test is not uniformly weak, so family A's answers stay as good as their SQL, and this run understates how badly a fully-8B assistant would do. It measures what an 8B ROUTER does with capable tools, which is the quantity the optimizable surface actually addresses. Stated so no reader takes the baseline for a small-model assistant.

known_gaps.what: The seed's parse-failure rate on this student is 3.0% rather than registration 2's 0.0%.
known_gaps.effect: Up to 3% of baseline rollouts contribute a `parse_failure` rather than an answer. It is reported per arm and never folded into answer accuracy, and a candidate that reduces it is credited as improving format rather than reasoning.

known_gaps.what: test_unseen lost about 39% of its rollouts in both arms of registration 2 to `upstream` cache misses, on a split of seven templates.
known_gaps.effect: test_unseen supports description and not inference, which §7 already required of it.
